security.notes: All Phase 2 handlers in src/main/ipc/app.ts call assertRendererFrame(event) BEFORE any logic, then .parse() input through Zod, then .parse() output before returning. tests/unit/main/ipc/app.spec.ts asserts every handler returns its system module's mocked output AND that malformed input is rejected BEFORE the system module is called (vi.mocked(...).not.toHaveBeenCalled() on every reject row). The deep-link parser (src/main/system/protocol.ts) defensively re-parses its own output through DeepLinkPayloadSchema and never throws on garbage input — verified by tests/unit/main/system/protocol.spec.ts (every malformed URL returns null, no throws). The protocol contract's allowlist (only repo/<slug>, settings, action/<id>) is now regression-tested — any drift in the regex grammar fails a test. issues.description: Global accelerator path is NOT driven E2E. The `CommandOrControl+Shift+Space` global shortcut and the macOS native menu Cmd+K accelerator both require an OS-level keypress to fire (Electron's globalShortcut and Menu accelerator subsystems hook the OS event loop, not the renderer keyboard). Playwright's `page.keyboard.press()` injects keystrokes into the renderer, not the OS. We unit-test the handlers behind those accelerators (spotlight show/hide, registerActions → installNativeMenu) and exercise the in-app renderer fallback for Cmd+K via the keyboard-shortcuts hook in palette-flow.spec.ts. A real-OS E2E would need a CI runner with accessibility permissions and an OSAScript / AppleScript helper to synthesise a system-wide keystroke. Deferred to a future hardening pass.

Tray right-click → recent-repo flow is NOT driven E2E. The tray is an NSStatusItem (macOS) backed by `Tray` in Electron; clicking it from Playwright would require both visible tray rendering and OS-level click coordinates. The tray's webContents.send → renderer route (`tray:on:open-repo`) is covered by the TrayOpenRepoPayloadSchema schema tests + the use-tray-open-repo-bus unit interaction (covered indirectly by the registry tests). Adding a real tray E2E is deferred — same OS-keypress / OS-click constraint as the global-accelerator gap above.

The renderer-level Cmd+K fallback (src/renderer/components/layout/keyboard-shortcuts.tsx) is only mounted inside the catalog shell. On /settings the in-app Cmd+K does nothing — Cmd+K only works there via the native macOS menu accelerator (which is correctly installed by app:registerActions but cannot be driven from Playwright). The palette-flow.spec.ts test was structured to verify Esc-close BEFORE Enter-navigate so both behaviours are pinned on the catalog route where the renderer fallback is live. Consider lifting the Cmd+K binding to the root layout (App.tsx) so the in-app fallback works on every route; the action registry already has app.open-command-palette as a global-scope action.

Carried over from Phase 1: production Electron build is not yet automated-tested for the case where a non-allowlisted file:// URL is requested — the sender-frame allowlist is verified only as an inspected property. Recommended Phase 3 follow-up: add a Playwright spec that pokes a malicious file:// URL via webContents.loadURL and asserts the assertRendererFrame() rejection path fires.

Carried over from Phase 0/1: tests/unit/main/ipc/system.spec.ts still uses a dynamic string-import for the handler module so the suite remains importable when src/main/ipc/system.ts is missing. The handler is stable now (Phase 0 ship); a tidy-up pass should switch to `import { handlePing } from '@main/ipc/system'` and drop the @vite-ignore.

The dispatchAction sync-throw branch is documented but not exhaustively tested — the registry intentionally only catches async rejections (handlers that return a rejected Promise). Synchronous throws from a handler bubble up to the dispatch caller (palette / menu / deep-link bus). registry.spec.ts now pins the async-reject branch; if a future contract change demands sync-throw resilience, add a try/catch around the handler invocation in registry.ts and update the test.

Carried over from Phase 1: native-module ABI flip persists. `pnpm electron:rebuild` builds better-sqlite3 + find-git-repositories against Electron's NODE_MODULE_VERSION; running `pnpm test` afterwards against host Node breaks the legacy DB-backed specs. Today's workflow: `pnpm rebuild better-sqlite3 find-git-repositories` for vitest, then `pnpm electron:rebuild` for Electron E2E. Worth a `test:full` script that orchestrates both rebuild flips around the suites.

Carried over from Phase 1: tests/e2e/catalog-flow.spec.ts intentionally does NOT exercise the scan flow — a real scan needs git-repo fixtures + Ollama. The new palette-flow.spec.ts inherits the same constraint. A real-scan E2E with a temp tree of bare-git-init repos is still recommended for a future hardening pass.

Carried over from Phase 1: double SearchBar on `/` and duplicate Settings link in top-bar + sidebar still present. Phase 2 did not regress these but did not fix them either. UX cleanup item — pick one owner and drop the duplicate.
